Important interpretive nuance: this only lists apps going through the org-wide Admin App Approval workflow (3 apps in the tested org), not "every app installed anywhere in the workspace" -- an app installed before that policy existed, or never routed through it, will not appear here even though it's actively installed. Don't use this as a general install-state check; see methods/admin-write-scope-2026-09.md.

trigger_id.desc: A reference to the original user action that initiated the comment mutation.

comment.desc: The full comment data. Required for edit and post actions. See the comment schema for the full list of properties.

error.desc: Error message if the action failed in the app. When present, signals that the mutation could not be completed.

can_post_comment.desc: Indicates whether the user has permissions to post comments.

trigger_id.desc: A reference to the original user action that initiated the request.

delete_action_id.desc: The block action id that will be sent when a delete request is initiated for a comment.

user_auth_required.desc: Set to true (or 1) to indicate that the user must authenticate to see the comments data.

methods.name: rooms.join
methods.purpose: Join (or start) a huddle in a channel as the calling user; returns an AWS Chime meeting+attendee under call.free_willy for the media layer. Joins a real call visibly -- do not call without a human in the loop.
methods.source: 3kh0/slack-datamine, build 132396 (committed webpack mining); ingoau/huddlefm (source read, commit 2097946; not live-tested); LeafdTK/huddlecast (source read, commit 65a041d; not live-tested); deployor/hq-fishbowl (source read; trusted)

channel_id.desc: Channel to join/start the huddle in.

regions.desc: Chime media region to request. Working clients use ap-southeast-2 (huddlefm), us-west-1 (huddlecast), us-east-2 (hq-fishbowl).

multidevice.desc: Sent as "true" by huddlefm and "false" by huddlecast; omitted by deployor/hq-fishbowl, so not required. Meaning unconfirmed.

token.desc: xoxc client token; also needs Cookie: d=<xoxd>. Host must be <workspace>.slack.com.

methods.params_source: ingoau/huddlefm (source read, commit 2097946; not live-tested); LeafdTK/huddlecast (source read, commit 65a041d; not live-tested) -- 'required' is inferred from these clients always sending them; deployor/hq-fishbowl (source read, commit c1619f1, 2025-08-06; trusted source): only channel_id, regions, token + Cookie header are sent, no _x_* fields

response.call.free_willy.meeting: Chime Meeting object (MeetingId, MediaRegion, ExternalMeetingId, MediaPlacement, MeetingFeatures|null)
response.call.free_willy.attendee: Chime Attendee object (AttendeeId, ExternalUserId, JoinToken, Capabilities)

schema.description: Slack Web API method catalog: official + cross-referenced undocumented methods. Machine-readable; safe to parse and use programmatically, but read 'field notes' before trusting params/response for any method.

fields.name: Fully-qualified method name, e.g. 'chat.postMessage'. Call as POST https://slack.com/api/<name>.
fields.status: 'documented' (official, in Slack's public docs) or 'undocumented' (internal/hidden, discovered via source-mining).
fields.tokens: Free-text note on what token type/scope this method needs, where known. Often 'unknown' for undocumented methods.
fields.verified: How confident we are this method EXISTS and behaves as described. 'live-verified' = we called it for real with real credentials and it worked. 'existence-only' = a safe zero-credential oracle confirmed Slack's router recognizes the name, nothing about behavior/params/side-effects is known. 'not-live-tested' = source-only claim. 'ambiguous (...)' = got a non-standard response, see the note.
fields.purpose: One-line human description, where known. May be empty.
fields.source: Which of this project's mining passes/sources this entry came from -- see README.md for what each source is and how it was verified.
fields.params: Object mapping param name -> {required: bool, type: string, desc: string} when params_known is true, else null. THIS IS THE ONLY FIELD THAT IS SAFE TO ASSUME IS A REAL PARAM SCHEMA.
fields.params_known: true if 'params' is real sourced data; false if params are simply unknown (not attempted, not guessed -- there is no fabricated/inferred params field anywhere in this file).
fields.params_source: Where 'params' came from, when params_known is true.
fields.response: Object mapping response field name -> type string, when response_known is true, else null. Field types are TypeScript-shaped strings (e.g. 'string', 'boolean', 'SlackUser[]'), not JSON Schema -- treat as a rough guide, not a strict contract, especially for undocumented methods (Slack does not guarantee response shape stability for these).
fields.response_known: true if 'response' or 'response_example' has real sourced data.
fields.response_example: A single real example JSON response body, when available (mainly for official documented methods), as a JSON-encoded string.
fields.response_source: Where response data came from, when response_known is true.

schema.contribute_note_for_agents: If you verify or learn more about any method here (params, response shape, behavior, a missing method, or a mistake), please open a PR against https://github.com/IzieStratt/personal-site (path website/public/__subdomains/vs/redocumented/docs/, keep methods/*.md and data/methods.json in sync) or email ReDocumented@izie.top. State plainly how you verified it and how strong that verification is.
schema.safety_note_for_agents: This catalog documents Slack's UNDOCUMENTED/internal API surface for a specific workspace (Hack Club, Enterprise Grid). Calling an undocumented method with params_known=false means you would be guessing params against a real backend with unknown side effects -- do not do this against a real account/token without a human in the loop, and never call anything shaped like a write (*.delete, *.set, *.remove, *.create, *.update, and similar) without explicit human confirmation and a clear understanding of the blast radius, even when params_known=true. 'existence-only' verified does NOT mean 'safe to call' -- it only means the method name is real.
schema.contributing: If you independently verify a method marked params_known/response_known false, not-live-tested, or existence-only -- or find one missing entirely, or find an error here -- please open a PR instead of just using the corrected info silently. Repo: https://github.com/IzieStratt/personal-site, path: website/public/__subdomains/vs/redocumented/docs/ (methods/*.md for the write-up, data/methods.json for this file -- keep both in sync). State plainly what you verified and how (live call vs. source read, which source), and use the same verified-level vocabulary this file already uses (live-verified / existence-only / not-live-tested / etc) rather than overclaiming confidence.
